tireSize.title: Tire Size Calculator
tireSize.subtitle: Decode tire sizes, compare overall diameter and speedometer error, and check load index, speed rating and manufacture date.

input.title: Tire sizes
input.aHint: Type the size from the sidewall as is, such as 205/55R16 91V.
input.bHint: Enter a plus size or another size to compare it with A.

err.width: Width (first three digits) must be between 100 and 400 mm.
err.aspect: Aspect ratio (two digits after /) must be between 20 and 95.
err.rim: Rim diameter (number after R) must be between 10 and 26 inches.
err.li: Load index must be between 0 and 257.
err.speed: Speed symbol must be one of B to Y (e.g. H, V, W, Y).

result.label: {a} → {b}
result.headline: Diameter {pct}%
result.speedo: At 100 km/h on the speedometer you actually drive {actual} km/h

band.tight: Small difference, within the -2% to +1.5% range some countries accept as an exception. Still check that the size is approved by the vehicle maker first.
band.common: Within the commonly cited ±3%, but outside -2% to +1.5%. Check that the size is approved by the vehicle maker and does not rub the wheel arch.
band.over: The diameter differs by more than 3%. Speedometer error grows and the tire may touch the body. Make sure the size is approved by the vehicle maker.

result.loadLower: B's load index ({b}) is lower than A's ({a}). Never use a lower load index than the original.
result.speedLower: B's speed symbol ({b}) is lower than A's ({a}). Never use a lower speed rating than the original (snow tires are an exception).
result.noService: Add the load index and speed symbol (e.g. 91V) to compare load and speed ratings too.
result.svgAria: Tire side view: A diameter {a} mm, B diameter {b} mm
result.speedoHow: Assumes the speedometer is calibrated for tire A: actual speed = shown speed × B diameter ÷ A diameter.

inchUp.title: Plus sizes close to {a}
inchUp.desc: Same or wider width, within ±1.5% diameter, closest first. Tap to compare as B. Choose a tire whose load index is at least A's.
inchUp.none: No size with a similar diameter

result.disclaimer: Theoretical values from the size marking. Real diameter varies slightly by maker, model, wear and pressure. Before changing sizes, confirm with a shop that the size is approved by the vehicle maker.

share.text: {a} → {b}: diameter {pct}%, actual {actual} km/h at 100 km/h on the speedometer

dot.title: Tire manufacture date (DOT)
dot.desc: Enter the last four digits of the DOT code on the sidewall to see when the tire was made and how old it is.
dot.label: Last 4 digits of DOT
dot.hint: The first two digits are the week, the last two the year. e.g. 2524 = week 25 of 2024
dot.empty: Enter four digits to see the manufacture date here.

err.empty: Enter four digits to see the manufacture date here.
err.format: Enter the last four digits (week + year), e.g. 2524
err.week: The first two digits (week) must be 01 to 53.
err.future: That date is in the future. Please check the digits.
err.old: Three digits is a pre-2000 code. The tire is far older than 10 years, so replacement is recommended.

status.ok: Less than {check} years old. Check wear, cracks and pressure before worrying about age.
status.check: Over {check} years old. Have it inspected at least once a year and plan to replace it before {replace} years from manufacture.
status.replace: Over {replace} years old. Replacement is recommended even if it looks fine (spares included).

anatomy.title: How to read 205/55R16 91V
items: The aspect ratio is sidewall height as a percentage of width: 205 × 55% = 112.75 mm.
Overall diameter = rim × 25.4 + sidewall × 2. For 205/55R16: 406.4 + 225.5 = 631.9 mm.
Load index and speed symbols follow the table in Annex 1-2 of Korea's vehicle safety standards. 91 means 615 kg per tire, V means up to 240 km/h.
ZR marks a high-speed radial. The allowed speed is the symbol after it (e.g. 92Y).
XL (EXTRA LOAD, REINFORCED) is a reinforced tire built to carry more load at higher pressure.
A leading P marks a passenger tire (US style), LT a light truck tire and T a temporary spare.

inchUp.title: Before you plus-size
items: Lower the aspect ratio as the wheel grows so the overall diameter stays close to the original. A different diameter makes the speedometer disagree with real speed.
Never use a lower load index or speed rating than the original (Michelin).
Stick to sizes approved by the vehicle maker. Some countries only allow a -2% to +1.5% diameter exception.
The often-quoted ±3% is an industry rule of thumb, not an official standard.
Plus sizing can reduce ride comfort and fuel economy (Michelin FAQ).

dot.title: Manufacture date and replacement
items: The last four digits of the 'DOT' code on the sidewall are the manufacture date. 2524 means week 25 of 2024.
The date may be on one sidewall only. If you cannot see it, check the other side.
Inspect tires at least once a year after five years, and use them for at most ten years from manufacture (Michelin).
Replace any tire older than ten years, spares included (Continental).

season.title: Tread limit and winter tires
items: Tread depth must stay at 1.6 mm or more (Korean vehicle safety standards, Annex 1-2). Replace the tire when the wear indicators in the grooves show.
Winter tire compounds stay soft below 7°C, keeping grip in the cold (Hankook Tire).

items.a: Width 205 mm, aspect ratio 55% (sidewall 112.75 mm), radial construction (R), fits a 16-inch wheel, load index 91 (615 kg per tire) and speed symbol V (240 km/h). The overall diameter is about 631.9 mm.

items.q: How much can the diameter change when plus-sizing?
items.a: Use sizes approved by the vehicle maker. Michelin notes some countries only allow a -2% to +1.5% diameter exception. The common ±3% is an industry rule of thumb, so this calculator shows both ranges.

items.q: What happens to the speedometer with a bigger tire?
items.a: Each turn of the wheel covers more ground, so your real speed is higher than shown. Actual speed = shown speed × new diameter ÷ old diameter. A 1% larger tire means about 101 km/h at an indicated 100 km/h.

items.q: Can I use a lower load index or speed rating than the original?
items.a: No. Choose the same or higher. Korean standards also require a tire's maximum speed to be at least the vehicle's top speed (snow and temporary tires are exceptions).

items.q: Where is the manufacture date and how long do tires last?
items.a: The last four digits of the DOT code (week + year). Michelin recommends yearly inspections after five years and at most ten years of use. Continental also says to replace tires older than ten years.

items.q: What is the minimum tread depth?
items.a: Korean vehicle safety standards (Annex 1-2) require at least 1.6 mm of tread. Replace the tire when the wear indicators in the grooves show.

items.q: When should I fit winter tires?
items.a: Michelin recommends winter tires when temperatures fall below 7°C. Switch when it regularly drops below that.
